facts.name: Creeping Thyme
facts.color: Pink, lilac or magenta flowers over fragrant leaves
facts.light: Full sun; needs a dry, sunny spot
facts.notes: A fragrant evergreen mat smothered in tiny flowers in early summer. Takes light foot traffic, so it's good between stepping stones and along edges, and deer usually leave it alone. Needs sun and good drainage; it rots in wet soil.

sources.title: English Gardens (Metro Detroit garden centers): Creeping Thyme
sources.note: Sold at English Gardens (Thymus serpyllum), with Red Creeping Thyme and Woolly Thyme; 2 to 3 in tall, space 10 in apart.

sources.title: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox: Thymus serpyllum
sources.note: Creeping thyme is a low, woody evergreen grown as a groundcover, 2 to 3 in tall; trim it now and then to keep the stems from getting woody.

companions.why: Gardenia.net lists English lavender among the recommended companions for creeping thyme.
Gardenia.net lists sedum (stonecrop) among the recommended companions for creeping thyme.
